subject: Proposal: 36-month reserved commitment — seasonal true-up & safety net

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlashealth.com>

Cc: Ellen Roberts <ellen.roberts@atlashealth.com>

Subject: 36-month reserved ask + seasonal true-up question

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. We are evaluating a 36‑month reserved commitment for our inference spend (estimated baseline ~ $1.2M/year) and have a few asks from procurement to include in any proposal:

- A committed discount for a 3‑year term (procurement is pushing for 30–40% off list for the committed baseline).
- A seasonal true‑up mechanism (we have strong Q4 usage variance) so we don't overcommit for peaks but can still secure a long‑term rate.
- A safety buffer that credits us for spikes above the committed baseline (something like a percentage credit or usage bucket).
- Clarification on ramp schedules (how we can increase committed baseline year-over-year) and true‑up timing.

I've attached Atlas_RFP_questionnaire.pdf with some standard procurement fields. Can you propose a clean commercial that includes a sample ramp schedule and what an acceptable safety buffer would look like? Also include any required approvals we should expect from your side.

Ellen (procurement) is cc'd — she'll handle contract/legal questions.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Cloud Platforms
Atlas Health

Attachments: Atlas_RFP_questionnaire.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Ellen Roberts <ellen.roberts@atlashealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 36-month reserved ask + seasonal true-up question

Hi Sanjay — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFP. High level response below and I attached a working proposal (redwood_proposal_3yr.xlsx) and a simple pricing_model_36m.csv with the math.

TL;DR options we can offer today:
- Option A — 36-month prepay (single payment or annualized invoicing) with a 33% effective discount on committed baseline, staged ramp allowed (see schedule). Seasonal true‑up: quarterly true‑up with an annual reconciliation; overages above the committed baseline receive a 20% credit applied to the following quarter's committed invoice.
- Option B — Annual reserved commitment with a 36‑month price lock and tiered discounts (Year1 35%, Year2 32%, Year3 30%) — more flexible but slightly smaller up‑front concession.

Proposed ramp schedule for Option A (example):
- Year 1 committed baseline: 100% of agreed baseline ($1.2M)
- Year 2: option to increase commitment up to +25% with 90 days' notice (price tied to original discount tier)
- Year 3: final increase up to +20% with 90 days' notice

Safety buffer proposal: 15% seasonal buffer where usage between 100–115% of committed baseline is charged at committed rate but credited 50% of the overage cost back to the customer as a credit on the next invoice. Above 115% is billed at pay‑as‑you‑go list + no credit. This protects Atlas for normal seasonality while keeping tail risk shared.

Notes on approvals: discounts >30% require pricing committee sign‑off and finance + legal coordination for prepay terms. If you like Option A at 33%, we’ll route for expedited approval but will need a one‑pager justification (strategic logo + volume certainty).

I'll coordinate internally with KarThik and Grace on the formal approval path — cc'd. If this looks promising I'll send a DocuSign link and a clean SOW.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Karthik / Rishi —

I'm okay greenlighting a 33% effective discount for a 36‑month reserved commitment with the following conditions:
1) Atlas must commit to at least two joint customer references or a joint case study during Year 2 (marketing participation).
2) Require finance to accept the seasonal credit mechanic as an accounts‑receivable credit (no cash refund) and limit total credits in any contract year to 10% of that year's committed invoice.
3) Legal needs a standard prepay SOW and a one‑page summary that outlines ramp rights and true‑up cadence.

If those conditions are acceptable I'll sign off and ask Finance to expedite the accounting review. Rishi — once you have a signed LOI we can finalize the exact discount and marketing terms.

Sanjay — thanks for the clear brief. Good news: we can proceed with a practical commercial that balances Atlas's desire for a deep multi‑year discount and our need to manage tail risk. Summary of the agreed path (pending LOI):

- Commitment: 36‑month reserved commitment on an agreed baseline (example baseline $1.2M/year).
- Discount: 33% effective discount on committed baseline (subject to LOI and legal/finance signoff).
- Ramp: Yearly increase options (Y2 +25%, Y3 +20%) with 90 days' notice; increases keep the original discount tier.
- Seasonal true‑up: Quarterly true‑ups, annual reconciliation.
- Safety buffer: 15% buffer where usage up to 115% is billed at committed rates and Atlas receives a 50% credit on the overage amount applied against the next invoice; credits capped at 10% of committed invoice per contract year (per Finance's request).
- Conditions: Atlas to provide two joint references/case study by Year 2 (marketing), and contract structured as a prepay SOW with the above true‑up language.

Next steps: I've attached the redwood_proposal_3yr.xlsx and pricing_model_36m.csv for numbers + a short one‑pager we will send to pricing committee. If that looks good to you, we'll issue an LOI and route the deal to Legal + Finance for final signoff. Once Legal confirms SOW language I'll send a DocuSign link.
